info.Class:Weaveshaper:
WEAVESHAPER An elf chants in an ancient library, listening to the whispers of the story stones around her. Ribbons of arcane energy form around her blades each time she cuts at the air, gathering her power in practice for what must be done. A human man clad in red and black faces a massive golem of cloth and necromantic magic. He summons a strange sword to his hands while calling to the arcane eye bound upon his magical outfit. In a flash of light the outfit transforms into a suit of fantastical armor covered in blades. With incredible speed, he launches forward and lashes out at the nightmare with a barrage of attacks, cutting and cleaving. A dwarf gestures, weaving a massive bladed mace from arcane thread as massive mechanical armor grows around her. The oncoming orcish horde heistates for just a moment, and that’s all the time she needs to break them. A tiefling cloaked in darkness spins a web of shadowy string between his hands. As a tavern brawl begins, he stands and demands that the violent patrons take their fight elsewhere, coiling tentacles of dark shadowsilk writhing in the air around him. Frightened, the combatants quickly flee, never seeing the tiefling’s bladed cloak twitch ominously. These are weaveshapers: warriors who pursue magical and martial perfection by creating powerful weapons called threadblades. By infusing their bodies with countless fragments of arcane energy from every school of magic, they strive for perfection through cunning artifice and martial study rather than introspective meditation or exploration of the more traditional arcane arts. WOVEN BLADES There is a certain power in harmony and unity between the arcane disciplines. Weaveshapers seek to harness this unity and instill within themselves the same eerie perfection. Thus, they train their bodies and minds to work in unison, learning to weave threads of arcane energy comprised of the many different strands of arcana. The first act that defines the weaveshaper is the creation of a threadblade. By memorizing the complex gestures and mental states required to invoke arcane thread, the weaveshaper can create powerful weapons with strange and majestic forms. These weapons are known as threadblades, as they appear to be woven from strings of magic. The sharpened edges and eerie blades of these wicked tools are crafted by conjuring thin panes of raw force around compressed arcane thread, leading to colorful and powerful expressions of each weaveshaper’s personal style. SKIN AND SKEIN Once a weaveshaper masters the creation of their threadblade, the next step is the creation of an arcane infusion. By weaving arcane energy into their clothing and bodies, these magical warriors begin to ascend to a higher physical and mental state. The most common manifestation of this power is a set of remarkable garb, which layers over the weaveshaper, providing strength and durability through magical enhancement. Unlike monks, who harness the natural power of ki within themselves, weaveshapers rely on arcane mastery and knowledge to empower their bodies to the peak of perfection. PERSONAL TAPESTRIES Each weaveshaper has a unique taste and style, as all creative artists do, and so they learn to create mystical accessories to compliment their infusions and threadblades. These can manifest in a variety of ways, from sentient eyes of woven cloth or cloaks of living blades to massive mechanical armor and illusory tomes of arcana. The threadblade may be a masterwork that binds them, and infusion is an art often discussed, but conversation regarding these personal implements is rare by custom. UNIFIED PATTERNS Despite the varying threadblades, infusions, and tapestries of the weaveshapers, the methods for unleashing arcane might during combat is rigid, structured, and subject to much scholarly discussion. The arcane essence of a threadblade naturally aligns to a peculiar set of attacks, one following another to weave a resulting rush of magical energies. Some patterns empower the body of the weaveshaper, allowing one to strike with swiftness and surety, while others unleash elemental forces or conjure other weapons. Many weaveshapers say their study is merely scholastic, but the results in battle are unquestionable and undeniable. CREATING A WEAVESHAPER When creating a weaveshaper, consider how you came to adopt this rare skill. Most weaveshapers train under tutors, learn in academies dedicated to the arcane arts, or are taught by entities bound to them due to the strange loom of fate. Why did you choose to continue down this path instead of learning traditional magic, for which you obviously have the aptitude? Is it due to restrictions placed upon you by your culture or your family? Is it by personal choice, seeing the mundane arcane arts as beneath you, or beyond your grasp? Do you endeavor to study both, and have merely started your journey here? Regardless, the path you’ve chosen is one that must be tread with careful consideration. QUICK BUILD You can make a weaveshaper quickly by following these suggestions. First, make Dexterity your highest ability score, followed by Intelligence, since it is essential when using your pattern attacks and when casting the spells you gain later. Then, select the Scissorblade. Finally, choose a background that would present you with an opportunity to study the arcane arts. CLASS FEATURES As an weaveshaper, you gain the following class features. HIT POINTS Hit Dice: 1d8 per weaveshaper level Hit Points at 1st Level: 8 + your Constitution modifier Hit Points at Higher Levels: 1d8 (or 8) + your Constitution modifier per weaveshaper level after 1st PROFICIENCIES Armor: None Weapons: Simple weapons, martial weapons Tools: Weaver’s tools and one stringed musical instrument Saving Throws: Dexterity and Intelligence Skills: Choose two from Acrobatics, Arcana, Athletics, Deception, Insight, and Sleight of Hand EQUIPMENT You start with the following equipment, in addition to the equipment granted by your background: (a) a scholar’s pack or (b) an explorer’s pack a set of fine clothes a set of weaver’s tools THE WEAVESHAPER

info.Subclass:Crimson Couturier:
Crimson Couturier

Your tapestry manifests as an eye of living thread and arcane intelligence, bound to your infusion. It is sentient and can speak with you, though it is merely a reflection of your own subconscious knowledge. You pour your own blood into this tapestry as you fight, and it grants you speed, strength, and endless determination. Fight as one, and find your way.

Couturier Arts (Level 3)

When you choose this tapestry, you also learn certain spells. You can cast each of these spells once, and you regain the ability to cast them when you finish a long rest.

Crimson Couturier Spells

LevelSpells
3rddetect magic
4thdarkvision
7thspeak with dead
10thlocate creature
13thtelepathic bond

Fresh Blood (Level 3)

At 3rd level, you create your tapestry and begin to feed it with your blood and power, demanding it to grow alongside you. You can use this accessory as a weapon to make melee spell attacks that deal slashing damage equal to 1d12 + your Intelligence modifier, causing blades, fangs, and razor edges to spring from your outfit and strike. If this attack hits and the target is grappling you, you can free yourself automatically. If you are grappling your target, this attack is made with advantage.

Unstoppable Duo (Level 6)

At 6th level, your connection to your tapestry allows you to perform impossible feats. You gain a bonus to Strength checks and saving throws equal to your Weave Tier, and when you take the Dash action, your jumping height and distance increases to equal your walking speed.

Rise As One (Level 10)

At 10th level, your tapestry demands your body act, even when it has been broken. You can stand from prone without using movement at any time during your turn and you can use your Clothier’s Cleave attack even while you are unconscious. Additionally, your Renaissance Regular feature’s stairway or bridge can now reach up to 60 feet.

Fearless Flight (Level 14)

At 14th level, you connect perfectly with your tapestry and unlock the power within your infusion, transforming it into a form far greater than before. While you are wearing no armor, you gain a flying speed equal to your walking speed and you can’t be frightened.
info.Subclass:Mortal Couturier:
Mortal Couturier

You are different from other weaveshapers. You view your threadblade as the ultimate accessory, so you seek to master every form it can take. You store your research in a floating, illusory tome that follows at your shoulder, holding your infinite array of threadblades within. Your struggle is an endless one, for to wear weapons of war is to become war itself. Glory to mortality, for everything that lives is designed to end.

Couturier Arts (Level 3)

When you choose this tapestry, you also learn certain spells. You can cast each of these spells once, and you regain the ability to cast them when you finish a long rest.

Mortal Couturier Spells

LevelSpells
3rddetect evil and good
4thlevitate
7thsending
10tharcane eye
13thteleportation circle

Tome of Blades (Level 3)

At 2nd level, your tapestry stores your threadblade research. You gain access to a second threadblade form, chosen from the threadblade list. You can change both your threadblade forms when you finish a short or long rest. You can summon either threadblade immediately before making an attack. Choose one or more of your threadblade forms each time you select them. These threadblades use your Intelligence ability score modifier for attack and damage rolls, instead of your Strength or Dexterity.

Shards of Light (Level 6)

At 6th level, your tapestry allows you to fragment your form into illusions. When you take the Dodge action, you create false figments of your form that move alongside you until the start of your next turn. The first time you are targeted by a creature’s attack during this time, it must first make an Intelligence saving throw. If it fails, the attack automatically misses.

Illusory Evasion (Level 10)

At 10th level, you can nimbly dodge out of the way of certain area effects, such as a red dragon’s fiery breath or a fireball spell. When you are subjected to an effect that allows you to make a Dexterity saving throw to take only half damage, you instead take no damage if you succeed on the saving throw, and only half damage if you fail. You can have your Renaissance Regular feature’s stairway or bridge be illusory, or illusory to all creatures except you.

Glory Eternal (Level 14)

At 14th level, you gain access to all categories of threadblades, and can summon any of them at any time. You can use either your Dexterity or your Intelligence to attack with them, and you can’t be stunned or paralyzed.
info.Subclass:Starspiral Couturier:
Starspiral Couturier

Your tapestry is woven from the light of the stars themselves, forming an armor around your body. It is strangely mechanical, yet smooth and comforting. Powered by your will and your brilliant arcane energy while moving in tandem with your body, this suit acts as an extension of your infusion, allowing you to stride across the battlefield as a massive harbinger of hope and destruction. Listen to the stars, and pierce the heavens.

Couturier Arts (Level 3)

When you choose this tapestry, you also learn certain spells. You can cast each of these spells once, and you regain the ability to cast them when you finish a long rest.

Starspiral Couturier Spells

LevelSpells
3rdalarm
4thsee invisibility
7thdispel magic
10thbanishment
13thdream

Face of War (Level 3)

At 3rd level, your tapestry surrounds your infusion like armor and provides you with deadly ranged attacks to supplement your threadblade. You can use this accessory as a weapon to make ranged spell attacks at a range of 120 feet that deal force damage equal to 1d10 + your Intelligence modifier, launching explosive stabbing missiles from your arcane mechanisms. This attack isn’t made with disadvantage if your target is prone, and deals twice as much damage if your target is Huge or larger.

Massive Machine (Level 6)

At 6th level, you can choose to increase the size and power of your tapestry. You can use your action to become Large for 1 minute, or to return to normal size. While you are Large or larger, you gain advantage on Strength checks and saving throws, and whenever you take damage, you can reduce the damage you take by 2, after any resistances.

Galactic Body (Level 10)

At 10th level, your tapestry protects you from the strange spaces beyond the world. You no longer need to breathe, you gain resistance to necrotic and radiant damage, and you are immune to poison. Your Renaissance Regular feature’s stairway or bridge can now be big enough to be easily traversable by Huge or smaller creatures.

Heaven Piercer (Level 14)

At 14th level, you finish your tapestry, unlocking its ultimate form. When you use your Massive Machine feature, you can choose to become Huge instead of Large. While you are Huge or larger, your reach for all melee weapons increases by 5 feet, and you can reduce the damage you take by an amount equal to 2 + your Intelligence modifier (minimum 3).
info.Subclass:Shadowsilk Couturier:
Shadowsilk Couturier

Your tapestry is far closer to its namesake than most others, manifesting as a cloak embroidered with razor-sharp blades and imbued with potent illusion magic. It moves at your command, twitching, grasping, and cutting at your leisure. You aren’t entirely sure if it obeys your conscious thoughts or your subconscious mind, but either way, it is always watching your back. Raise your hood, or raise your blades.

Couturier Arts (Level 3)

When you choose this tapestry, you also learn certain spells. You can cast each of these spells once, and you regain the ability to cast them when you finish a long rest.

Shadowsilk Couturier Spells

LevelSpells
3rdcharm person
4thinvisibility
7thmajor image
10thblack tentacles
13thseeming

Cloak of Blades (Level 3)

At 2nd level, your cloak moves to defend you and strike at your foes. You can use this accessory as a weapon to make melee spell attacks at a reach of 15 feet that deal slashing damage equal to 1d8 + your Intelligence modifier, causing cutting blades to lash from your cloak. If you hit a creature with this attack, you can choose to force it to make a Strength saving throw. If it fails, it is pulled to the nearest open space within 5 feet of you.

Hidden Agenda (Level 6)

At 6th level, your cloak conceals your movements and distorts your speech at your command. You can choose to have your speech be incoherent to creatures other than those you choose. When you take the Dash action, you can choose to gain the benefits of the Disengage action as well.

Grasping Dark (Level 10)

At 10th level, your tapestry grips the environment around you, holding you aloft. You gain a climbing speed equal to your walking speed, and you can move along walls and ceilings while leaving your hands free. You can have your Renaissance Regular feature’s stairway or bridge be invisible.

Shadow Dance (Level 14)

At 14th level, your cloak’s blades tear at the fabric of reality, opening tiny portals for you to slip through. After you perform a Weave Finisher, you can teleport up to 15 feet to a location you can see. Also, whenever you take the Dodge action and a creature misses an attack targeting you, or a creature you can see ends its turn, you can use your reaction to teleport up to 15 feet to a location you can see.
